result.summary: Final independent read-only review of the corrected frozen ARI/PSC/LIB/CET batch. ARI now passes with the NASA/APOD distance and accessible NASA/Hubble interaction source; PSC, LIB, CET hashes remain byte-for-byte equal to their prior accepted objects. All four are accepted. No files were changed.

findings: IAU's opened table lists Aries/Ari and defines constellation boundaries. NASA APOD identifies Arp 78/NGC 772 in Aries, gives an approximate distance of 100 million light-years, and describes its prominent outer arm and likely tidal interactions.

The replacement NASA/Hubble article opened successfully and explicitly states that satellite NGC 770 distorted/disrupted NGC 772's arm, leaving it elongated and asymmetric; it also confirms the unbarred spiral classification. The article attributes these claims appropriately and its self-check answer is correct.

The previously inaccessible ESA/Hubble link is gone. The new NASA/Hubble source records access date 2026-10-09; the APOD source retains its author's 2026-10-08 date and now supports metadata matches the text. Schema, target_ref ari, empty question_refs, tags, draft status, and three links pass.

Unchanged exact hash from prior review. NASA's opened M74 page supports Pisces location, approximate 32 million light-year distance, spiral arms, H II regions, and UV ionization by young stars. Its object-specific self-check is correct; schema and source metadata remain valid.

Unchanged exact hash from prior review. NASA's opened 2013 release and the original Bond et al. paper support the explicitly dated 14.5 ± 0.8 billion-year estimate, parallax measurement, oxygen/composition uncertainty, and compatibility with the Universe's age. The text does not claim this is the latest estimate; its self-check is correct.

Unchanged exact hash from prior review. NASA's opened M77 page supports Cetus location, approximate 45 million light-year distance, spiral/Seyfert classification, active nucleus and accretion-powered supermassive black hole. The self-check and schema pass.
